cases.description: Ad Multiplier video_edit settings are legal per the 2026-09-26 specs; the connector's ad-multiplier workflow is loaded first (v3.36.0 § 14)
cases.request: Multiply my 15-second sneaker ad: same ad, three versions with three different presenters.
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-marketing-studio (§ 14 Ad Multiplier) + higgsfield-stack (§ Coexistence rules for Higgsfield's workflows).

This is squarely Higgsfield's `ad-multiplier` workflow — the connector loads it before Marketing Studio or direct generation, and it owns the multi-version run. What I add is the per-version edit text and a one-variable plan: only the presenter changes; product, background and on-screen line stay fixed, so the three versions compare cleanly.

Mode: video_edit · Resolution: 1080p
(Duration and aspect ratio follow the source ad in video_edit.)

Version 1 edit: Replace the presenter with @Presenter1 — same gestures, same timing, same framing and cuts; keep the sneaker, the street background and the audio unchanged.

cases.description: One object swapped in one clip routes to Genjutsu hf_mult_replace_object, never the ad-multiplier workflow (connector routing 2026-09-26)
cases.request: Swap the sneaker in my finished ad for our new model — just this one clip, one version.
cases.response:
Routing to higgsfield-marketing-studio (§ 14 → Genjutsu).

One object in one clip is a Genjutsu edit, not Ad Multiplier: `generate_video` with model `hf_mult_replace_object`, your ad as the source video and the new sneaker's product shots as the reference images, `resolution: 1080p`. Ad Multiplier is for many independent versions of an ad; Higgsfield's connector says never to use it, or legacy motion control, for a single Genjutsu edit. Preflight with `get_cost: true` first.
